report.tagline: India's bike taxi app that grew into the biggest challenger to Uber and Ola, with cheap rides on bikes, autos and cabs.
report.simpleSummary: Rapido lets you book a ride on the back of a motorbike, often for half the price of an auto, which is perfect for one person beating city traffic. It now also offers autos and cabs and has a food delivery app called Ownly. Instead of taking a cut of every fare like Uber, Rapido charges many drivers a small daily or per-ride subscription fee, so drivers keep the full fare. That helped it win drivers and riders fast, and it is now valued at $3 billion.

overview.whatItDoes: Rapido is a ride-hailing app founded in Bengaluru in 2015 by Aravind Sanka, Pavan Guntupalli and Rishikesh SR. It started with bike taxis, then added autos, cabs, parcel delivery and, from 2025, food delivery through Ownly. Uber's CEO has said Rapido overtook Ola as Uber's biggest rival in India.
howItWorks: A rider picks bike, auto or cab and sees the fare upfront.
Drivers, called Captains, get the request on the Rapido Captain app and accept it.
For bike, auto and cab, many Captains pay a subscription (a fixed daily or per-ride fee) instead of a percentage commission, so they keep the fare.
Riders pay by UPI or cash directly to the Captain in many cases.
Bike Captains use their own two-wheelers; helmets are provided for riders.
Ownly lets users order food with low menu prices because restaurants pay lower commissions.
overview.valueProposition: For riders: the cheapest, fastest way through traffic for one person. For drivers: keep the full fare by paying a small fixed fee instead of a big cut.

painPoints.pain: Traffic makes cars and autos slow and costly for one person
painPoints.howSolved: Bike taxis weave through traffic at a fraction of cab fare.

painPoints.pain: Auto drivers refusing trips or demanding extra money
painPoints.howSolved: Upfront fares in the app and quick matching.

painPoints.pain: Drivers losing 20 to 30% of fares to commissions
painPoints.howSolved: Subscription model lets Captains keep the fare for a fixed fee.

painPoints.pain: No ride-hailing options in smaller cities
painPoints.howSolved: Rapido operates in 400+ cities using cheap bike supply.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Book a motorbike ride; the Captain gives you a helmet.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Rapido's original and cheapest product; drives high ride frequency.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Drivers pay a fixed fee per day or per ride rather than a percentage.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Wins drivers from Uber and Ola, which brings faster pickups for riders.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Book autos and cars, including Cab Economy.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Makes Rapido a full ride app, not just bikes.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Food ordering with lower commissions for restaurants and lower prices for users.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: A step to a super app and more uses for the same riders and Captains.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: SOS button, ride sharing with contacts, Captain verification.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Builds trust for riding on a stranger's bike.

steps.detail: Chooses bike for speed and price.
Checks number plate and OTP; gets a helmet.
Pays by UPI to the Captain.
Signs up with licence and vehicle papers.
Chooses a daily subscription instead of commission.
Keeps the fares minus the fixed fee.
Sees Ownly in the Rapido app.
Finds a biryani cheaper than on Swiggy or Zomato.
Orders again if the food and time were good.

businessModel.summary: Rapido earns mainly from Captain subscription fees and commissions, plus delivery fees on parcels and food. Delivery earnings now outpace ride-hailing in its revenue mix.

revenueStreams.detail: Fixed daily or per-ride fees paid by drivers on autos, cabs and bikes in many cities.
Percentage cuts on some ride types and markets.
Parcel and food delivery fees; this part grew faster than rides in FY25.
Ads in the app and brand tie-ups.

businessModel.pricing: Bike fares often start around ₹25 to ₹40 base plus distance; short trips commonly cost ₹40 to ₹80. Autos and cabs cost more. Captain subscription fees are small fixed amounts that vary by city and vehicle (not fully public).
costDrivers: Rider and Captain incentives and discounts
Legal costs from state bike taxi rules
businessModel.unitEconomics: On a ₹60 bike ride, a Captain on subscription keeps nearly all of it. Rapido earns only a few rupees from that ride via the subscription, but costs per ride are also low because it does not handle payment or pay big incentives once Captains are busy. Rapido makes money when Captains do many rides a day, so a fixed fee covers its costs. The FY25 loss of ₹258 crore on ₹934 crore revenue means it still spends more than it earns, mostly on growth and ads (estimate).

howTheyGetUsers: Lowest price option on most short trips
Large ad campaigns, including cricket and TV
Word of mouth among students and young workers
whatBringsUsersBack: Cheap fares versus autos and cabs
Fast pickup due to many Captains
Using one app for rides, parcels and food
growth.moat: Rapido has the largest bike taxi supply in India, and its subscription model makes Captains prefer it. More Captains mean faster pickups and more riders, which is a network effect. Its low-cost model also makes it hard for Uber and Ola to match prices without losing money.

competitors.name: Uber
competitors.positioning: Global ride-hailing leader in Indian metros with Moto, Auto and cabs.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Rapido is cheaper and offers zero commission to drivers; Uber has more premium cabs and stronger brand trust.

competitors.name: Ola
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Rapido overtook Ola as Uber's main rival, with better driver economics.

competitors.name: Namma Yatri
competitors.positioning: Zero-commission open-network auto app strong in Bengaluru.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Rapido has bikes, cabs and food and is in many more cities.

competitors.name: Swiggy and Zomato (for Ownly)
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Ownly charges restaurants less and is much smaller.

improvementIdeas.idea: Rider-side cancellation guarantee with instant credit
Women-only Captain option in more cities
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More women riders and rides at night.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Share of rides by women riders

Bundle Ownly savings with ride passes

improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More food orders from existing riders.

pmLessons: Winning supply wins a marketplace. Rapido's zero-commission plan pulled drivers, which made pickups fast and rides cheap.
A cheaper product for a specific need, one person in traffic, can beat bigger rivals.
Regulation can be existential. Bike taxis depend on state rules.
Expanding to a super app works best when it reuses the same users and drivers.

interviewQuestions.question: Why did Rapido's subscription model work for drivers?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare commission vs fixed fee for a busy driver. Talk about predictability, earnings and how that improves supply.

interviewQuestions.question: A state bans bike taxis. What do you do as PM?
interviewQuestions.hint: Protect users and Captains: shift to autos and parcels, work with regulators, track ride loss and Captain churn.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you improve safety for women riders?
interviewQuestions.hint: Research concerns, propose features like women Captains, live tracking, check-ins. Measure share of women riders.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Rapido build food delivery?
interviewQuestions.hint: Weigh synergy (users, Captains) vs costs and strong rivals. Suggest a focused test and metrics.

interviewQuestions.question: Pick a north star metric for Rapido.
interviewQuestions.hint: Completed rides per week. Break into riders, Captains, completion and cross-use.
